name: São Paulo
tagline: From two-Michelin-star Amazonian cuisine to the mortadella sandwich that made The New York Times.

D.O.M.description: Contemporary Brazilian cuisine from chef Alex Atala, with Amazonian ingredients. Two Michelin stars, 9th-best restaurant in the world on The World's 50 Best. Anthony Bourdain dined here with Atala in the São Paulo episode of "The Layover" (2012).

Fasano.description: A reference for Italian tradition in São Paulo, considered by many the city's number-one restaurant. Critic Josimar Melo (Folha de S.Paulo) calls it "the most professional of all, impeccable in every aspect you'd expect from a restaurant."

Maní.description: Signature cuisine from chef Helena Rizzo, one of Brazil's most awarded chefs. One Michelin star.

Hocca Bar.description: The legendary mortadella sandwich from the Mercadão, created in 1952 and even featured by The New York Times.

Picchi.description: 100% Italian, family-style cuisine from chef Pier Paolo Picchi, in Jardins. One Michelin star.

A Casa do Porco.description: São Paulo's temple to pork, from chef Jefferson Rueda. Consistently ranked among Latin America's best restaurants by The World's 50 Best, with a guaranteed line at the door.

Evvai.description: Chef Luiz Filipe Souza's Italian-rooted tasting-menu cooking, holder of one Michelin star. One of the most celebrated addresses in Jardins.

Mocotó.description: Chef Rodrigo Oliveira's restaurant, which elevated sertanejo and northeastern Brazilian cooking to fine-dining status, on the edge of the city's far north. A regular on The World's 50 Best Latin America lists.

Bar da Dona Onça.description: Chef Janaína Rueda's bar and restaurant at the foot of Oscar Niemeyer's Copan building. Popular Brazilian cooking with a contemporary touch, repeatedly voted the city's best bar.

Consulado Mineiro.description: The definitive reference for Minas Gerais cuisine in São Paulo, with hearty dishes like tutu à mineira and canjiquinha.

Consulado da Bahia.description: Bahian flavors in Pinheiros since 2010: acarajé, moqueca and shrimp-stuffed pumpkin, from the same group behind Consulado Mineiro.

Jun Sakamoto.description: One of Brazil's most celebrated sushi counters, led by Japanese chef Jun Sakamoto. Top-tier omakase in Vila Nova Conceição.

Aizomê.description: Chef Telma Shiraishi's signature Japanese cooking; she also produces an award-winning line of artisanal soy sauces and vinegars.

Kinoshita.description: Japanese kappo cuisine with one Michelin star, founded by Toshio Kinoshita in Vila Nova Conceição.

Sujinho.description: Traditional Bela Vista boteco famous for its generous steaks and no-frills atmosphere, open late into the night.

Famiglia Mancini.description: Iconic Italian-São Paulo institution in Bela Vista, with all-you-can-eat pasta and antipasti on Rua Avanhandava, heart of the city's 'Little Italy.'

Speranza.description: One of the most traditional trattorias in Bixiga, the neighborhood synonymous with Italian immigration to São Paulo.

Bar Léo.description: Historic Bixiga boteco known for beer served in chilled clay mugs and dishes like oxtail stew (rabada).

Vinheria Percussi.description: A pioneer of food-and-wine pairing in São Paulo, with a list of over 300 labels and chef Silvia Percussi's heartfelt Italian cooking. Recognized by the Michelin Guide.

Bráz Pizzaria.description: The pizzeria that helped establish Neapolitan-style pizza in São Paulo, with its iconic filet-and-catupiry pie.

Pizzaria Castelões.description: One of São Paulo's oldest pizzerias, founded in 1924 in Bixiga, a symbol of the city's Italian tradition.

Bar do Mané.description: Historic rival to Hocca Bar inside the Mercadão, also claiming the title of creator of the mortadella sandwich.

Coffee Lab.description: One of the pioneers of specialty coffee in São Paulo, founded by Brazilian barista champion Isabela Raposeiras.

Suplicy Cafés Especiais.description: São Paulo roastery and café that pioneered Brazil's specialty-coffee movement, with traceable beans from partner farms.

Padaria Bella Paulista.description: 24-hour bakery that's a São Paulo icon, its display case packed with breads, pastries and savory snacks that draw locals and tourists at any hour.

Feira da Liberdade.description: Traditional weekend street fair on Praça da Liberdade, with Japanese and Nikkei food stalls in the neighborhood with the largest concentration of Japanese descendants outside Japan.

Sushi Yassu.description: One of the oldest Japanese restaurants in Liberdade, serving traditional cuisine since the 1970s.

Fogo de Chão.description: The rodízio steakhouse that became one of Brazil's biggest culinary exports, with servers carving prime cuts tableside.

Guilhotina Bar.description: Signature cocktail bar in Pinheiros built around Brazilian botanicals. Has ranked among Latin America's best bars on The World's 50 Best Bars list.

Bar Balcão.description: Bohemian Jardins bar built around its iconic 25-meter zigzag counter. A gathering spot for artists and intellectuals since 1994.

Django.description: New Orleans-inspired restaurant and bar in Vila Madalena, with live music, craft beer and dishes like ribs and gumbo.

Tordesilhas.description: A menu that travels across Brazil's regions in one sitting, in Jardins, with dishes like paçoca de pilão and baião de dois.

Rubaiyat.description: Reference steakhouse for prime cuts in Jardins, part of a group that raises its own Black Angus cattle.

Veloso.description: Vila Mariana favorite famous for its meat pastel served with sugarcane juice or caipirinha, repeatedly named one of São Paulo's best pastéis by local critics.

Ponto Chic.description: Historic spot on Largo do Paissandu, birthplace of the Bauru sandwich, created there in the 1930s and named after a regular customer.

Bar Brahma.description: Historic bar founded in 1948 on the corner of Avenida São João and Ipiranga, a landmark of downtown São Paulo nightlife, immortalized in a Caetano Veloso song.

Bar do Juarez.description: São Paulo bar chain born in Vila Madalena, known for its burgers and linguiça sausage boards.

Grazie a Dio!.description: Vila Madalena boteco-trattoria with a relaxed vibe and generous Italian dishes meant for sharing, popular with expats.

Mercado Municipal de São Paulo.description: The 'Mercadão,' a historic market opened in 1933 with stained glass by Conrado Sorgenicht, famous for its exotic fruit, codfish pastel and mortadella sandwiches.

Corrutela.description: Sustainability-driven tasting-menu restaurant in Pinheiros from chef César Costa, with its own composting and solar power. Listed on both The World's 50 Best Discovery and the Michelin Guide.

Metzi.description: Contemporary Mexican cooking in dialogue with Brazilian ingredients, from chefs Luana Sabino and Eduardo Nava Ortiz, both alumni of Cosme in New York. Featured on The World's 50 Best Discovery.

Carlota.description: Restaurant from chef Carla Pernambuco, one of the pioneers of female-led fine dining in São Paulo.

Namesa.description: Vila Madalena restaurant built around its iconic communal table that winds through the dining room, favoring light, seasonal dishes.

Barbacoa.description: Popular rodízio steakhouse chain among São Paulo's business crowd, with a full buffet and prime cuts.

Habib's.description: Arab fast-food chain founded in São Paulo in 1988, today one of the largest of its kind in the world and a popular symbol of Arab cuisine in Brazil.

Mercado de Pinheiros.description: Traditional neighborhood market, smaller and more informal than the Mercadão, famous for its codfish fritters and Argentine-style empanadas.

Santo Grão.description: Café and restaurant on Rua Oscar Freire with its own coffee roast, a meeting point on Jardins' main shopping strip.

Empório Alto de Pinheiros.description: Boteco-grocery in Alto de Pinheiros with one of the city's most complete craft beer and cachaça lists.

Z Deli.description: Jewish delicatessen founded in 1981, a reference for Ashkenazi Jewish culinary tradition in São Paulo, with dishes like gefilte fish and varenikes.

Jardim de Napoli.description: Traditional Italian trattoria open since 1949, famous for its mozzarella-stuffed polpettone, an absolute classic of Italian-São Paulo cooking.

La Casserole.description: French bistro founded in 1954 by a French immigrant couple on the picturesque Largo do Arouche, with dishes like cassoulet and steak tartare.

Arábia.description: A reference for Arab and Lebanese cuisine in São Paulo since the 1980s, with dishes like raw kibbeh and strained yogurt.

Skye Bar.description: Rooftop bar and restaurant atop the Ruy Ohtake-designed Hotel Unique, with a red pool and panoramic views of Ibirapuera Park and the São Paulo skyline.

Spot.description: Classic Jardins restaurant that helped establish brunch culture and a relaxed vibe among São Paulo's creative class since the 1990s.

Camarada Camarão.description: Shrimp-focused chain born in Recife, with over 50 shrimp recipes on the menu and a location on Avenida Paulista.

Bar Original.description: Laid-back Vila Madalena boteco, a traditional outdoor happy-hour gathering spot in the bohemian neighborhood.

Cervejaria Nacional.description: São Paulo craft brewery with a brewpub in Vila Madalena, part of the movement that drove Brazil's craft beer scene.

Dalva e Dito.description: Heartfelt Brazilian cooking from Alex Atala and Alain Poletto in Jardins, recognized by the Michelin Guide.

Terraço Itália.description: Restaurant atop the Edifício Itália, one of the city's tallest buildings, with 360-degree views over São Paulo.

Bar Estadão.description: 24-hour boteco in downtown São Paulo, a traditional hangout for journalists from the O Estado de S. Paulo newspaper, famous for its draft beer and pastéis.
